## Morning Briefing: Friday, October 30, 2026

Friday is a transit corridor, not a working day. You are in Austin for the Principled Business Summit, which runs until 12:30 today, and you leave the hotel before dawn for a 07:00 flight, so the summit's closing morning happens without you. From 08:19 to 14:42 you belong to DFW airport, and the only two live meetings on the calendar, the Sales and Recruiting standup and the GEHC AI Routing technical dive, both get taken from a gate area. Neither is accepted. That matters more than usual because today is the Friday you named as the deadline for the AI Practice 2027 decisions with Curtis, and tomorrow is the day Rock 3's KR2 on account-increase tracking comes due. The quarter's two hardest commitments land on the one day this week you have no desk, no focus block, and no buffer longer than 56 minutes.

The item most likely to slip is the AI Practice 2027 plan. The reminder built to protect it came due yesterday and is now a day late, and its own notes name today as the Friday deadline, so the runway it was designed to buy is already spent. Five decisions are still open for Curtis, from first-year direct revenue range to what you personally stop doing, and with none of them recorded there is no one-page charter for the Dec 1-2 session and no clean path to the Dec 15 signature. Behind that, Rock 2's South Texas gap decomposition was due October 17, Chase owns it, and no completion exists anywhere, which is what a zero-row delegation tracker looks like from the inside; Rock 3's KR2 lands tomorrow and Rock 1 has no recorded progress since it was committed. Two external deadlines press on the same hours: YPO wants officer identification and a strategic focus pillar by tomorrow, and Rock 5 is the thing you said you would settle today. And there is no daily review for yesterday in reviews/daily/ or in Obsidian, so the written record of what you decided on the road stops at October 28.

Three things need watching. Both timed meetings are tentative and one is a client session with thin recent context: the GEHC deeper dive has had no client touch since September 18, and four items are still open, including whether Braunstein expects self-tuning routing, a question that has survived three separate notes. Run Chase prep before 10:00 if you want anything beyond those four items. The travel logistics also carry two live conflicts: the Hilton is booked through October 31 while checkout is today, and the Birmingham trip overlaps the Libby and Patrick visit that starts today. Clay reminders and birthdays are unavailable this run, so any relationship obligation living there is invisible until it bites, though the Jarvis folder is genuinely empty and nothing routed through it is waiting. What makes today a success is narrow: the five decisions recorded before you land in Birmingham, and nothing else. Treat the airport hours as a decision room, not as email time.
